title: Workload Weaver — continuous batch parameter synthesis, probe canaries, and safe rollback
creator: Isabella Martinez
description:
Goal: Build 'Workload Weaver', a service that continually synthesizes candidate batching configurations from sampled production telemetry, evaluates them via an offline replay simulator and short-lived probe canaries, and provides a safe-apply / rollback controller that enforces latency, error, cost, and quality guards. This ticket scopes the core inference path integration, offline evaluation harness, canary runner, and rollout rules for automatic safe apply.

Motivation: Current batching autotuners produce static suggestions and require manual validation. Teams need an automated loop that: 1) learns parameterizations per workload cohort (max_batch_size, microbatch cutoff, kv_window, batching window), 2) predicts cost/latency tradeoffs with an offline replay, 3) validates a minimal real-traffic probe, and 4) either promotes the config or triggers rollback. The Weaver aims to reduce unit token cost by 8-20% for stable workloads while preserving p99 latency and generation quality.

Scope:
- Telemetry schema extensions: additional workload fingerprint fields and sequence length histograms.
- Offline replay engine: deterministic replay of traces with a simulated runtime to estimate latency and cost deltas.
- Heuristics synthesizer: generate candidate parameter sets using profile-driven rules + small hill-climb search.
- Probe canary runner: apply candidate on <1% traffic with shadow logging and limited time window.
- Safe-apply controller: rollout policies, automatic rollback triggers, and audit logs for every apply.
- Integration points: routing layer for traffic slices, console dashboard for recommendations, and API to accept/deny proposals.

Out-of-scope for this ticket: user-facing UX polish beyond the console prototype, broad A/B experimentation framework, and enterprise RBAC for apply actions (will be follow-ups).
acceptance_criteria: Telemetry schema updated and consumers instrumented (histogram + fingerprint tags)
Offline replay can run a 24h trace in <2h and produce cost/latency estimates within 10% of real run for holdout workloads
Heuristics synthesizer returns ranked candidate configs with expected delta metrics
Probe canary runner can apply a config to a 0.5-1% traffic slice, collect shadow traces, and produce pass/fail signals
Safe-apply controller enforces: p99 latency regression < 10%, error-rate increase < 0.1 percentage points, cost change bounded by policy, and automatic rollback on breach
Console shows a recommendation card, confidence score, and one-click 'schedule probe' action
All applies are recorded with an audit entry (who/when/params/metrics)
implementation_notes: Telemetry: extend existing trace proto with 'weaver_fingerprint' (cohort id), length_histogram (buckets: 1-32,33-128,129-512,513+), and hint tags for response type (chat/complete/embedding)

Replay: reuse request-replay infra from ENG-612345 but add a lightweight runtime model that approximates KV cache hits and batching coalescence behavior; initial simulator uses conservative latency multipliers per kernel path

Synthesizer: seed initial candidates using heuristics (percentiles of observed batch sizes, typical sequence lengths) then run a local hill-climb with budgeted iterations to avoid combinatorial explosion

Probe runner: implement as a route-level override in the routing service; attach a shadow-mode where results are logged for replay comparison without affecting production outputs until success is declared

Safe-apply controller: state machine with phases (proposal -> probe -> evaluation -> promote/rollback). Evaluation compares probe metrics against baseline windows and offline predictions. Add exponential backoff for repeated failures
Data retention: store sampled traces for 30 days for replay accuracy; anonymize identifiers before storage
CI: add unit tests for synthesizer heuristics and integration test for probe lifecycle using synthetic workloads

risks: Simulator mismatch: offline replay may under/over-estimate p99 leading to unsafe promotes. Mitigation: conservative multipliers and mandatory probe stage.
Quality regressions: cost-driven configs may increase hallucination/quality drift. Mitigation: integrate eval prompt set and quality checks before promote.
Operational blast radius: automatic applies without tenant-aware guards could affect SLAs. Mitigation: tenant opt-in and canary caps per region.
Data privacy: sampled traces may contain PII if not sanitized. Mitigation: require anonymization pipeline and TTL enforcement before retention.
rollout_plan: Phase 1: internal canary on staging routes with synthetic workloads and offline replay validation (2 weeks). Phase 2: limited production probe (0.5% traffic) for selected cohorts with human approval gates (3 weeks). Phase 3: automated safe-apply for non-customer-facing cohorts with 24h observation window and auto-rollback enabled (4 weeks). Post-mortem and metrics review before wider rollout.
